Settlers cost 10% less [ICON_Gold] Gold to purchase. Domestic [ICON_TradeRoute] Trade Routes sent from a city with a Suguba provide +2 [ICON_Production] Production. +1 [ICON_TradeRoute] Trade Route capacity for each continent on which you own at least three cities that you founded (maximum +4).

Every tile of a city that holds at least one Wonder has +1 Appeal. In a city with a Grove, +5% [ICON_Production] Production toward Wonders for each Breathtaking tile adjacent to the Wonder being built, up to +20% (counted at the start of your turn). Great Wall segments adjacent to another segment provide +1 [ICON_Faith] Faith.

Cities you found on Hills gain +1 [ICON_Production] Production and +10% [ICON_Production] Production toward Settlers. They also gain +25% [ICON_Production] Production toward districts until their first specialty district is complete.

Unimproved Rainforest tiles adjacent to a Preserve provide +1 [ICON_Culture] Culture once Medieval Faires is known. Cities with at least three Rainforest tiles gain +10% [ICON_Production] Production toward Wonders. Once Medieval Faires is known, each Rainforest in a city that holds at least one Wonder provides a further +1 Appeal to adjacent tiles.

Settlers have +1 sight. The first [ICON_TradeRoute] Trade Route sent from each city you found claims up to two unowned tiles near that city (checked at the start of your turn). International [ICON_TradeRoute] Trade Routes sent from a city with at least one Camp or Pasture provide +2 [ICON_Food] Food and +1 [ICON_Production] Production.
Cities with a Lavra gain +20% [ICON_Production] Production toward Settlers. Cities you found on Tundra or Tundra Hills receive a free Builder. Tundra Woods provide +1 [ICON_Food] Food.

+30% [ICON_Production] Production toward Preserves. +10% [ICON_Production] Production toward a Wonder that is adjacent to a Breathtaking tile (counted at the start of your turn). Unimproved Breathtaking tiles adjacent to a Wonder provide +1 [ICON_Culture] Culture. Every tile of a city that holds a National Park has +1 Appeal.

Every tile of a city in which a Château is adjacent to a Wonder or a Preserve has +1 Appeal (checked at the start of your turn). Châteaux adjacent to a Wonder or a Preserve provide +1 [ICON_Production] Production. +10% [ICON_Production] Production toward a Wonder that is adjacent to a Château (counted at the start of your turn).

The caravans of Mali carry more than salt and gold: they carry the next city. Buy your Settlers, plant them on every shore you can reach, and let the trade that binds them together pay for the ones that follow.
A Wonder is only as fine as the land that frames it. Tend the groves, choose each site as a painter chooses where the mountain stands, and the empire itself becomes the garden.

From the high plateau every valley looks like an invitation. Found your cities where the ground rises, and each one will be quick to raise its first quarter and quicker still to send out the next band of settlers.
Leave the forest standing and it will repay you. Under its canopy rise Wonders the world will cross oceans to see, and every one of them makes the green around it lovelier still.
No wall marks where the Cree nation ends. Send your Traders out along the rivers and across the plains, and the land they cross will come to know your name. Let every new camp begin with a caravan.

Beyond the last village the forest goes on, and beyond the forest the snow. Others see empty land; you see room. Raise your Lavras, send the settlers east, and make the cold country feed an empire without end.

A canyon, a waterfall, a marble dome set just where the valley opens: a nation can be composed like a painting. Keep the wild places wild, build beside them with care, and the whole country becomes a park worth crossing the world to see.

A palace is never one building. It is the avenue that leads to it, the water that mirrors it and the gardens that make a visitor forget the road home. Lay out your Châteaux first, and let each Wonder rise as the centrepiece they were waiting for.
